question: Under the NTEP DOTS framework, which of the following correctly describes the role of the 'treatment supporter'?

answers.text: A healthcare worker who administers all doses of anti-TB medication in hospital under direct supervision.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Hospitalisation for DOTS is not the norm. The treatment supporter is typically a community-based individual — a family member, ASHA worker, or community volunteer — who observes the patient swallowing each dose at home or in the community.

answers.text: A community-based individual (ASHA worker, trained community volunteer, or trusted family member) who directly observes the patient swallow each dose of ATT.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The DOTS treatment supporter is a community-based person who directly observes each dose being swallowed. This ensures adherence without requiring hospitalisation and is the cornerstone of NTEP's community-level TB control.

answers.text: A district TB officer who reviews treatment cards monthly at the DOTS centre.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The district TB officer performs supervisory and administrative functions. The treatment supporter is the person who directly observes the patient take each dose.

answers.text: A pharmacist at the designated DOTS centre who dispenses monthly drug supplies to the patient.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Drug dispensing is separate from observed treatment. The treatment supporter's defining function is direct observation of each dose swallowing — not dispensing.

overallFeedback.feedback: Revisit the NTEP programme structure section. The treatment supporter directly observes each dose being swallowed — typically an ASHA worker, community volunteer, or trained family member — forming DOTS' community infrastructure.
Correct. Community-based direct observation by a treatment supporter is the practical heart of DOTS under NTEP.
